html:
SMTO-GWT-0088 — The Gateway is at its limit for jobs or saved data

GUID: fa218520-c520-570a-83a4-749e6b6d470f
Slug: gateway-state-capacity
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • The Gateway limits how many jobs it runs at once, how much job history it keeps, and how big one request can be. This request would go over a limit, so the Gateway turned it down.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check your conversations for Tasks still running on this Gateway, and stop any you no longer need. Running jobs count against the Gateway's limit, so fewer of them frees room for new work.
  2. If this request handles a lot of data at once, split it into smaller parts. One request's saved record can be too big for the Gateway's per-request limit.
  3. Once running jobs have finished, send your request again. The Gateway turned it down without starting it, so it is safe to send again once there is room.

What success looks like

  • The request starts on the Gateway and the Task shows it running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway; they can raise its limits. Don't delete the Gateway's saved job history to make room; it is what stops jobs from running twice.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway admission or state validation hit a configured resident-state limit (event subscribers, request size, total or active jobs, per-record or total bytes), or a GATEWAY_RAM_* limit was set below its safe minimum.

What this means

  • Admission or state validation exceeded an event-subscriber, execution-envelope, job, active-work, per-record or total-byte limit, or configured a bound below its safe minimum. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Admission or state validation exceeded an event-subscriber, execution-envelope, job, active-work, per-record or total-byte limit, or configured a bound below its safe minimum.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the specific exhausted bound and distinguish a single oversized record from too many jobs or subscribers; retain existing work.

How to fix it

  • Identify the limit from the message (for example "Gateway RAM admission capacity reached", "record capacity", "byte capacity", "event subscriber capacity", or "<NAME> is below the safe minimum"). Let active jobs finish or reduce the request size; if capacity planning requires it, stop the Gateway and raise GATEWAY_RAM_MAX_JOBS, GATEWAY_RAM_MAX_ACTIVE, GATEWAY_RAM_MAX_RECORD_BYTES or GATEWAY_RAM_MAX_BYTES (defaults 120000, 1000, 1 MiB, 1 GiB; minimums 1, 1, 64 KiB, 1 MiB) before restarting. Do not delete retained job records to make room.
  • Reduce the specific oversized request or observer load, or let owned work settle. Change supported state limits offline only when capacity planning requires it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The relevant bound is satisfied through smaller valid requests, settled work or an explicit supported offline capacity change.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
